//: Turbo façade for geoai-core. This file exists so turbo can reach the package; every command it runs is a Python tool from the pixi environment, and the commands themselves belong in the package's pyproject.toml and pixi.toml. Three rules make it work. (1) Always `cd` to the repository root first: ruff's `src` and pytest's `testpaths` in pyproject.toml are absolute-from-root, so a command run from inside python/geoai-core resolves neither. (2) Every Python tool is reached through `pixi run -e default --`. Turbo itself is a Bun-workspace package and therefore exists only in the `bun` environment; QGIS and the interpreter exist only in `default`. The `-e default` is what crosses that boundary, and it is explicit because a nested `pixi run` inherits the ambient environment and would otherwise look for `python` in the bun environment. (3) Never invoke a tool through node_modules/.bin — those entries carry a `node` shebang, and no environment in this repository provides node; bun is the only JavaScript runtime. Keys prefixed `//` are the convention for commenting in package.json: bun parses it as strict JSON, so a raw `#` comment is a syntax error.
name: @geoaiworkbench/core

scripts.test: cd ../.. && pixi run -e default -- python -m pytest python/geoai-core/tests -q
scripts.lint: cd ../.. && pixi run -e default -- ruff check python/geoai-core && pixi run -e default -- ruff format --check python/geoai-core
scripts.fmt: cd ../.. && pixi run -e default -- ruff check --fix python/geoai-core && pixi run -e default -- ruff format python/geoai-core
scripts.cov: cd ../.. && COVERAGE_FILE=.coverage.geoai_core pixi run -e default -- python -m pytest python/geoai-core/tests --cov=geoai_core --cov-report=xml:python/geoai-core/coverage.xml --cov-report=term-missing

//cov: COVERAGE_FILE is not optional. turbo runs all three cov tasks concurrently in the same working directory, and coverage's default data file is the single path ./.coverage — so the three runs interleave writes to one SQLite file and each report ends up containing every package's numbers (observed: geoai-core's report listing all three packages, geoai-mcp's listing two). The numbers stay plausible, which is the dangerous part: nothing looks wrong, the merged total is just wrong. One data file per package is the fix; a per-package data_file in pyproject.toml would work too but is invisible at the point where the collision happens. It is exported on the command line rather than inside the pytest args because the process that has to see it is the activated environment, not pytest.
